stories.headline: Naidu directs officials to brace for another cyclone
stories.title: Naidu directs officials to brace for another cyclone
stories.summary: Depression over Bay of Bengal likely to intensify into cyclone; rain forecast in South Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Amaravati: Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu has directed officials to accelerate restoration works in areas affected by Cyclone Arnab and simultaneously take advance precautions against another impending cyclone.
He called for coordinated action to restore normalcy and strengthen the state’s preparedness for further rainfall.
Officials informed him that a depression over the southeast Bay of Bengal was likely to intensify into a cyclone by Sunday.
Moderate to heavy rainfall was forecast in South Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema on November 2, 3 and 4.
The Chief Minister reviewed the weather situation and post-cyclone restoration works with senior Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) officials at the Secretariat.
He asked officials to prepare plans for effective rainwater utilisation through better water management.
Concerned about communication disruptions during power outages, Chandrababu directed officials to install diesel generators at all mandal headquarters to keep mobile networks operational.
He called for alternative power arrangements for all 4,500 BSNL towers and towers operated by other telecom service providers.
He also asked officials to explore Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) options.
Officials informed the Chief Minister that 7,000 personnel were engaged in electricity restoration in Cyclone Arnab-affected areas.
He directed them to speed up the work and ensure that every household received power supply.
He also ordered the immediate restoration of cyclone-damaged roads and reconstruction of the protection wall near Kakinada.

stories.headline: India's opposition set to hold mega rally seeking election chief's resignation
stories.title: India's opposition set to hold mega rally seeking election chief's resignation
stories.summary: It comes amid growing protests over a voter roll revision exercise feared to leave 130 million voters off rolls.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Tens of thousands of people are expected to gather in the Indian capital, Delhi, for a mega opposition rally, seeking the resignation of chief election commissioner and electoral reforms.
The rally, called by the main opposition Congress party, will begin around noon at the famous Ramlila Maidan grounds, with leaders claiming a million people could attend.
Several top leaders of the Congress-led INDIA alliance have said they would attend and the influential Gen Z-led pressure group Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has also pledged support.
The rally comes amid growing criticism of a voter-list revision exercise that has removed 130 million names from the draft rolls across India.
The Election Commission of India (ECI) says the exercise is aimed at updating the voters' list by purging names of people who have died or moved away from their registered addresses.

But opposition parties allege that the exercise - known as the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) - could benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) by removing eligible voters from the rolls.
They accuse the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and the BJP of "vote chori (theft)".
Both the BJP and the ECI have denied the allegations.

The controversy intensified in September when The Indian Express newspaper in its investigation, external reported that the CEC, Gyanesh Kumar, made key decisions related to the exercise without the agreement of the two other election commissioners, who had raised objections on more than a dozen occasions.
The Election Commission said differences of opinion were normal in any institution and did not affect its functioning.
But concerns over the revision process have continued, with the opposition parties, the CJP and student groups organising a number of protests in Delhi and other Indian cities.

Last month, Congress MP and leader of the opposition Rahul Gandhi led tens of thousands of protesters in a march from Connaught Place in central Delhi to the Supreme Court, seeking the CEC's resignation.

stories.headline: IOA’s election Code of Conduct bars criticism of ‘private life’ of candidates, publicity
stories.title: IOA’s election Code of Conduct bars criticism of ‘private life’ of candidates, publicity
stories.summary: The election to pick 10 members of the Athletes' Commission of the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) will be held on November 3, while the polls to choose eight SOMs will be held on November 9
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: No criticism of opponents’ “private lives”, a bar on all forms of publicity, including the use of new media and social networks, and a requirement for IOA and NSF office-bearers to maintain neutrality feature in the Model Code of Conduct for the upcoming elections to the Athletes’ Commission and Sportspersons of Merit (SOMs).
The election to pick 10 members of the Athletes' Commission of the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) will be held on November 3, while the polls to choose eight SOMs will be held on November 9.
Both elections will be held virtually, and separate instructions will be issued later by Electoral Officer Sanjay Kumar Srivastava.
There are 12 candidates — including Olympic medallists P.V. Sindhu and Mirabai Chanu — in the fray for the Athletes' Commission membership.
The 10 members — five men and five women — will be elected by the 34 members of the electoral college — two each from 17 National Sports Federations (NSFs).
Eight SOMs — four men and four women — will be elected from among 80 SOMs — 40 men and 40 women — notified by the Electoral Officer.
Some of the legendary figures of Indian sports, including incumbent IOA President P.T. Usha, are in the fray to become one of the eight SOMs.

"A candidate shall not produce any spoken word, written text or representation of any nature likely to harm the image of another candidate or cause him prejudice, and criticism of other candidates, if made, shall be confined to their policies and programme, past record and work," one of the provisions of the Model Code of Conduct said.

"The promotion of a candidate shall exclude any form of publicity, including the use of new media or social networks, and no public meeting or gathering of any kind may be organised in the process of promoting a candidature.”
"NSF and candidates shall refrain from criticism of all aspects of private life, not connected with the public activities of the athletes.
No candidate shall engage in criticism based on unverified allegations or distortion against any other candidate, and there shall be no appeal to caste or communal feelings for securing votes."
The Model Code of Conduct also prescribed that electoral campaigns shall be carried out by the candidates in a fair manner and, in a spirit of respect for fundamental ethical principles.

stories.headline: J&K budget discussions for 2027-28 to begin Nov 16
stories.title: J&K budget discussions for 2027-28 to begin Nov 16
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 31: The Jammu and Kashmir government has set November 16 as the starting date for departmental budget discussions for the financial year 2027-28, directing administrative departments to furnish five-year revenue trends, outstanding liabilities of ongoing projects, staffing details and measurable development targets as part of a detailed examination of their financial proposals. According to an official communication issued by the Finance Department on Saturday, accessed by Rising Kashmir, the discussions will cover Revised Estimates for 2026-27 and Budget Estimates for 2027-28 under both revenue and capital components, including Centrally Sponsored Schemes (CSS), the Prime Minister's Development Package (PMDP) and loan components. The exercise, scheduled to continue until December 2, will involve a department-wise examination of expenditure requirements, revenue generation potential, ongoing development projects and proposed financial allocations for the next fiscal year. The Finance Department has instructed all administrative departments to submit Action Taken Reports (ATRs) on previous budget announcements, wherever applicable, along with complete details of establishment expenditure and information relating to the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) framework. In a significant requirement, departments have been asked to disclose their sanctioned staff strength, employees presently in position and contractual manpower, bringing staffing requirements and associated expenditure into the budget discussions. The communication also requires departments to present scheme-wise trends in revenue and capital expenditure, along with revenue receipts recorded during the preceding five years and the scope for enhancing these receipts. Departments will additionally have to disclose the total liabilities of ongoing projects, details of major developmental initiatives and the key features of their proposed budgets. The Finance Department has specifically sought corresponding outputs, outcomes and targets against proposed allocations, indicating that departments will be required to explain the intended results of their expenditure proposals. Another requirement is the alignment of departmental budget proposals with the relevant Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), linking proposed financial outlays with broader development objectives. All departments have been directed to prepare detailed PowerPoint presentations in both soft and hard copies and furnish the required information well before their scheduled discussions. As per the official schedule, the exercise will begin on November 16 with the Disaster Management, Relief, Rehabilitation and Reconstruction Department, followed by Industries and Commerce and the Mining Department. On November 17, the Finance Department will examine proposals from Tribal Affairs, Information and Revenue departments, while School Education, Law and Justice/Election and Parliamentary Affairs have been scheduled for November 18. Jal Shakti (Public Health Engineering), Transport and Cooperatives will present their proposals on November 19. The following day, November 20, discussions will focus on Animal and Sheep Husbandry, Agriculture Production and Horticulture, three sectors with direct implications for the rural economy and livelihoods across Jammu and Kashmir. Hospitality, Protocol and Toshkhana/Estates, Youth Services and Sports/Technical Education (Skill Development), and Science and Technology have been scheduled for November 23. The Public Works Department, Housing and Urban Development and Jal Shakti (Irrigation and Flood Control) will face budget discussions on November 25. Rural Development, Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs, and Labour and Employment along with Stationery and Printing and ARI and Trainings have been scheduled for November 26. Tourism and Culture departments will present their financial proposals on November 27. On November 30, the discussions will cover Health and Medical Education, Fisheries and Planning, Development and Monitoring. The General Administration, Forest and Social Welfare departments have been scheduled for December 1. The exercise will conclude on December 2 with Higher Education, Power Development and Finance departments. The schedule places several major public-service and infrastructure departments, including education, healthcare, roads, drinking water, rural development and electricity, under departmental financial review ahead of the next budget. The Finance Department has also sought to limit physical participation in the meetings, directing administrative departments to ensure that only officers whose presence is absolutely necessary attend the discussions. Kashmir- and Jammu-based Heads of Departments and Deputy Commissioners have been instructed to participate through video conferencing. The demand for five-year revenue data, outstanding project liabilities and measurable expenditure outcomes will require departments to place detailed financial and performance information before the Finance Department as it examines proposals for the coming fiscal year.

stories.headline: Cybercrime, drugs among J&K’s biggest challenges: IGP Kashmir
stories.title: Cybercrime, drugs among J&K’s biggest challenges: IGP Kashmir
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 31: Inspector General of Police (IGP) Kashmir Sujit Kumar on Saturday identified cybercrime and the growing drug menace among the biggest challenges confronting Jammu and Kashmir, asserting that the police were prepared to tackle emerging threats while safeguarding national unity and security. Speaking to reporters at the historic Ghanta Ghar in Lal Chowk on the sidelines of Rashtriya Ekta Diwas celebrations, the IGP said the nature of challenges facing law enforcement agencies was evolving, with cybercrime and narcotics emerging as major areas of concern. “Cybercrime is one of the biggest challenges, both today and in the coming days. Along with the drug menace, there are other activities directed against our country, and Jammu and Kashmir is looking at these challenges from a new perspective,” Kumar said. He said the police would elaborate separately on the measures being undertaken to address these concerns, stressing that the occasion was dedicated to celebrating national unity and integrity. The Kashmir Police chief’s remarks came as security forces, police personnel, students and young people gathered at Lal Chowk to participate in National Unity Day celebrations marking the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. Describing Lal Chowk as a historic witness to the celebrations, Kumar said the gathering had provided an opportunity for people in Kashmir to join the nationwide observance of Rashtriya Ekta Diwas. “Today, we celebrated Ekta Diwas at historic Lal Chowk. We witnessed the live broadcast of the Ekta Diwas parade from Kevadia in Gujarat, where the Prime Minister addressed the nation,” he said. The IGP said Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha, personnel from Jammu and Kashmir Police and Central Armed Police Forces, schoolchildren and Kashmiri youth participated in the programme and listened to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's address. Referring to the Prime Minister's message, Kumar said the occasion had reinforced the responsibility of citizens and security agencies to protect the country's unity and integrity. “The Prime Minister has given us the responsibility of safeguarding the unity and integrity of the country. Whatever challenges come before the police and security forces in the coming days, we are prepared to face them,” he said. Asked specifically about the growing threat of cybercrime and the steps being taken to counter it, the IGP acknowledged the seriousness of the challenge but said a detailed discussion on the issue would be held separately. He also referred to the narcotics problem and activities threatening national security, indicating that the police were approaching these challenges with renewed focus. Kumar, however, emphasised that the immediate significance of the day lay in celebrating the country's unity and collective commitment to national integrity. “Today is the day of national unity, the day of the country's togetherness. We should celebrate it. I extend my greetings to everyone on National Unity Day,” he said.
